comments.author: Shinee
comments.body:
There are plenty of info available on jap wiki page and u can read up after translating.

Just a simple guide of the points for sharing, based on what I learned thus far.

1. Themes and general idea

This new game play is not for non-serious adventurers because the quests can only be performed if the char himself fulfils all the skill requirements. It is unlike normal adv quests and maps where only one fleet member needs to fulfil the requirement.

Each theme can have 1-3 relics to be found. Themes change with the period the game is in and there are special themes that only occurs based on selected historical events in play at the moment. Shining Hill is one such example now.

To find the relic, you must gather clues. Clues are ranked by stars and you can synthesise 2 types into potentially a higher ranked clue.

Higher rank clues can be "used" to obtain a corresponding Adv quest, once a day. Some of these quests are normal adv quests available from adv guilds while some are special quests associated to the relic storyline. In the case of the normal adv quest, you must fulfil the quest chain requirements on top of the skill requirements in order to undertake the quest from the clue.

You need to have a clue of suitable rank before u can obtain the Quest to discover the relic. Most relic quests are at the 15-stars Clue but some are known to be at 19 or even 20 stars. Fairytale theme has both relics at 15 stars, Hidden Hero is at 15 as well, Shining Hill has one at 15 stars and one at 19 stars.

2. Synthesising clues (or combining)

When synthesizing, you choose 2 clues of different types, one at a time. The first is like the main clue u wish to improve, the second is the ingredient u wish to consume in the process.

The outcome is either a success or a fail. If you fail, u lose all the clues u have chosen as the ingredient but you do not lose the main clue. If you succeed, u will gain a higher ranked clue. How much improvement you get depends on your ingredient. While i do not know the specific formula for it, a general rule of thumb i follow is to use at least 4x quantity of a clue for every level it is lower.

For example, if i am improving a 10 star clue, i will use at least 4x 9 stars clue as ingredient, 8x 8 star clues. or 12x 7 star clues.

3. How to get good clues

You get clues for almost everything u do in game. But the best method i found thus far is Archive and Reporting Discovery.

Using the Archives gives you a good amount of clues every time but to get high rank clues u need to have a high rank in any appraisal skills.

One important thing to note is that you only gain clues as high as the highest ranked clue you currently possess for the theme. Meaning, if your highest clue now is an 8-star clue, you will only get clues 8 stars and below.

Reporting discovery on the other hand, always gives the highest rank clues you can get. I usually reserve this method for clues above rank 12 where they are not common from archives.

comments.author: Visitor
comments.body:
Welcome. You can have most questions answered in-game on one of the three School chat rooms, which can be switched manually at any Beginner Academy's instructor NPCs. That said:

Blue quests are called "Chrono Quests". The first time you accept one, the game gives you the option of having a brief tutorial; in essence, the completion of Chrono quests rewards you with a title to access content in the game which might not be available ordinarily. That is the only difference between red and blue quests.

The numbers on a quest, meanwhile, indicated by an equivalent number of stars, represents its "difficulty" level. One star is the lowest and easiest difficulty, while ten stars represents the highest level of difficulty. Most quests can be done in any order you choose; some do unlock others as part of a sequence of quest chains, but their numbers have nothing to do with it.

There is much more to be learned, but you needn't try to take it all in at once. Be sure to consult the OGP forums' section on player-written guides for additional resources to help get you started. And may your time in the game be an enjoyable one.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
Atlantis. We've been waiting, and come December 8th will be, "Chapter 3: Acropolis", the next expansion of UWO in which we can finally seek out the truth of the legendary city. But every silver lining has its cloud -- access to the city and its wonders (items, memorial albums, and more) will likely follow the JP model, meaning it will only be around for a few months before it vanishes into the mists of obscurity, only reappearing and being accessible for brief periods of time.

So here's a nice checklist of Atlantis-accessing goals, which I think somebody should probably compile in the official UWO forum later (if they haven't done so already).

1. Graduate from any Intermediate school class: adventure, trade, or maritime. Proceed then to Amsterdam and meet with Mercator; accept the World Atlas quest, and chart the North Sea.
2. Discover Knossos Palace by completing the Legend of the Labyrinthos quest.
3. Unlock all your port permits through East Asia.
4. Visit Oxford to accept Land Survey quest from Professor Smith. Travel to Candia and chart the two landing zones, West Candia and Inland Crete.

This opens the path to the Atlantis story chains. Your next steps depend a bit.

Quest 1: Land of the Legendary King. All players can find it in Stockholm from the Adventure Mediator; if you've discovered the Siberian Husky (John Tradescant storyline quest), Amsterdam's Mediator also has it. If you've discovered Xanadu (John Tradescant storyline quest again), it's also-also found at London's Adventure Mediator.
Quest 2: Egypt and Atlantis. Comes from London's Adventure Mediator.
Quest 3: A Chance Encounter on the Sea of Atlas. Once again... London's Adventure Mediator.

From there, the Atlantis story branches out into Adventure, Trade, and Battle chains.

Adventure Chain: seems to require completion of the John Tradescant storyline. Not easily done; I couldn't find evidence of a special equip reward, but I may just have missed something.

Trade Chain: First quest ("A Certain Merchant's Worries") becomes available from Athens' Merchant Mediator after completion of the Land of the Legendary King. Takes place primarily in East Asia; grants the special EX equippable head accessory with "accident rate decrease Rank8" effect.

Maritime Chain: You have to complete the Henry Morgan quest chain, as well as the "Sea of Atlas" quest. Reward is a pair of cool EX boots with "melee combat force increase Rank1" effect.

If you want to try to track all of it, feel free to do so starting from Q#1: gvdb.mydns.jp/db/module/QuestDB/action/QuestShow?id=4958

Two other recommended resources:

gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?ImperialOrder (Imperial Quests to reach Atlantis will be required at certain times.)
gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?AncientTechnology (Special rewards involving Atlantis, certain game activities, and so on)

There's more, and who knows what will be altered for GAMA in the rewards department... but I really only wanted to give you the information needed to reach Atlantis; the rest we'll discover in time, and through the reports of other players, no doubt. Cheers, and great online voyaging to you all. And... sorry for taking over the front page like this.

We can ask OGP nicely to ask KOEI nicely to not take away our shiny precious Atlantean toy, but it's best to presume we will follow the lead of our Asian server cousins and see Atlantis leave in only a few months' time.

That aside, here's a nice checklist of Atlantis-accessing goals, which I think somebody should probably compile in the official UWO forum later (if they haven't done so already).

1. Graduate from any Intermediate school class: adventure, trade, or maritime. Proceed then to Amsterdam and meet with Mercator; accept the World Atlas quest, and chart the North Sea.
2. Discover Knossos Palace by completing the Legend of the Labyrinthos quest.
3. Unlock all your port permits through East Asia.
4. Visit Oxford to accept Land Survey quest from Professor Smith (you do NOT need to have started the Oxford thesis chain, only have East Asia permit, World Atlas from Mercator, and Knossos discovered). Travel to Candia and chart the two landing zones, West Candia and Inland Crete, then report back to Oxford for a reward.

This opens the path to the Atlantis story chains. Your next steps depend a bit.

Quest 1: Land of the Legendary King. All players can find it in Stockholm from the Adventure Mediator; if you've discovered the Siberian Husky (John Tradescant storyline quest), Amsterdam's Mediator also has it. If you've discovered Xanadu (John Tradescant storyline quest again), it's also-also found at London's Adventure Mediator.
Quest 2: Egypt and Atlantis. Comes from London's Adventure Mediator.
Quest 3: A Chance Encounter on the Sea of Atlas. Once again... London's Adventure Mediator. Beware of NPC sea battles (escaping is fine, as are Amulets of the Sun)
Quest 4: Aspiring a Pure World. Amsterdam Adventure Mediator.
Quest 5: Easiest one is Dangerous Caribbean from Seville's Maritime Mediator; a quick escapable/AoS sea battle, and you're good.

From there, report to your nation's palace, and speak with the secretary to complete the Solar Barca (three Imperial Quests; change weekly, vary in difficulty).

Atlantis does branch out into three distinct chains. They are:

Adventure Chain: Must have completed Xanadu discovery/John Tradescante episodes. Not easily done; I couldn't find evidence of a special equip reward, but I may just have missed something.

Trade Chain: First quest ("A Certain Merchant's Worries") becomes available from Athens' Merchant Mediator after completion of the Land of the Legendary King. Takes place primarily in East Asia; grants the special EX equippable head accessory with "accident rate decrease Rank8" effect.

Maritime Chain: You have to complete the Henry Morgan quest chain, as well as the "Sea of Atlas" quest. Reward is a pair of cool EX boots with "melee combat force increase Rank1" effect.

If you want to try to track all of it, feel free to do so starting from Q#1: gvdb.mydns.jp/db/module/QuestDB/action/QuestShow?id=4958

Two other recommended resources:

gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?ImperialOrder (Imperial Quests to reach Atlantis will be required at certain times.)
gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?AncientTechnology (Special rewards involving Atlantis, certain game activities, and so on)

Lastly, remember that GAMA contents/rewards may differ from paid subscribing servers. Sure hope not.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
A reason to return.... That really depends on your preferred style of play, doesn't it? Since that time, we've had:

New cities
New discoveries (in all fields, plus a special new category that requires no skill: Weather/Phenomena)
Time-specific recipes/items, and special titles that unlock them at your discretion
New equipment
New dungeon elements (including harder to fight land enemies)
New dungeons: The Labyrinth (Crete) and the Temple of Poseidon (Atlantis; only rarely accessible)
New stories, including the Atlantis saga
New maritime grinding options
New sea/land zones (including the Arctic North passages)
New ships (tons)
New weapon types (revolvers/crossbows)
New aide options (production/royal fleet/monthly fleet)
New ship skills

I don't keep track of specifics in Maritime ship strength, so I can't help you there. Further down the road, there'll be skills for pets, revamped Company Colonies, and of course, loads more new content, including a sister college to Oxford that'll make the game even more fun to play, and yet more ships/equipment/yadda-yadda.

I'd suggest dropping in and having a look around for yourself. If nothing else, maybe say 'hi' to folks who might remember you. Cheers, and fair winds to you, whatever your choice.

I saw the news myself just a bit ago. This is indeed a terrible turn of events; I can't honestly say I feel all that motivated to keep playing UWO at this point. It's possible this could still be reversed. October 18th is a few weeks away. But if not... well. I'll save that thought for another day. For now, I would recommend letting your voices be heard in the UWO forums. Maybe Vertigo, a company that claims it will "put users first, consistently reaching out to our gaming communities and keeping communication open" might hear us... and if KOEI-Tecmo is the one pulling these strings, so too might they.

... Later.

I worked so many hours to reach Rank 15 refined in all adventure skills, so many hours attacking NPC ships just to get Guard and gunnery refined and maxed again (I don’t even want to think of those who did them all). I never been a good producer, but those people who spent countless hours working to level up Sewing, Handicraft, Casting, trading skills, and oh god don’t forget Alchemy! I’m not even talking about Shipbuilding, Account, Marching, Rowing, Steering and definitely the most Overpowered skill Linguistic!! (Linguistic joke apart, all those skills, you’ll have to rework on them for many months).

As of the Adventure quests, I was about 85% of all quests completed, and I can tell you, I spent so much time sailing mindlessly, walking bore fully on lands, spending hours of using QMP just to finally find that impossible to find quest (I see you German footprint). I was a quest chain hunter, basically doing all quests that unlock another quest, trying to reach the end of each chains. Redoing all this work is a matter of a year! And that’s with the gear, character and ship I had! Now I’ll have to first work to get back a ship, skills and adventure gear for making things easier. (Oh God, I’m going to have to work again to become a Great Adventurer…)

Also, if they reset, many player will leave forever this game. Players who were supporting it, players working to make it nice, players who were there to help others. Reset the game, and I’m sure you’ll lose about 20 to 40% of old players. Not only will you lose old players, but you’ll also lose new potential players. Many new players live for like 1 week out of other players’ generosity since UWO start is harsh. They won’t be able to see what the game can really offer them, only seeing Barca everywhere and quit because they think the game is just too slow long and boring while in fact the game can offer you so much. You must also think that if you reset, many of the players who stayed but used to be pay player won’t be paying for the game anymore, felling like it’s just all dust in the wind. I’d say about 15% of the remaining players on the server will be (Technically, the % of player that won’t be paying is higher, I just don’t count the players who already left. Most likely, many of leaving players were people that used to pay but got mad getting all their money investment lost and who decided to never play the game again). Sure Uwo Economy suck right now, but do you think resetting the server will make things better? Things will just go back the same way if there’s no other changes than a reset.

But if you reset, you better solve Uwo problems and not just leave all the problems there. One of the well-known Uwo problem is that Ducats value is broken (It will be at one point on the restart). By broken I mean there’s a significantly higher % of money that’s made in the game than money spent. And that % is just crazy high. If you want to avoid it, you need to create appealing way for player to use their Ducats on NON Players stuff (Investment is nice, but definitely not enough). Examples. You could add a Special untradeable Ducats Ticket you can buy, I don’t know where (Major Cities?), which gives random loot with very low chances of ''good'' stuff. The more you invest into this ticket, the higher the chances it will give you something good. Limit it to a max of 1-3-5 times a day so people don’t abuse it too much. Add a World Ducats Donation weekly (Or others) reward, that when at end of that time period, everybody on the server get a bonus for the next time period (Example +10% skills points acquisition). Make the number atrocity high, expect that in the future, people will end up with more money (So making it like 100M is not a good idea for a high number, need to be higher than that by a lot). So either you make a super high donation number that cannot be broken by 1 single super rich player or you make it that each time the goal is reached the next goal is going to be upgraded to a higher number. (Or both together, but that’s just going to become an unused feature of the game if you do)

Also, there’s some small convenience that could be added to the game. A few of them: Make that Charioteer in Venice FINALY do something of his life and create a special carriage from Venice to Florence (Or Genoa, but Florence sound better). Even in old time there were more of a road between Venice/Florence/Pisa than Calais/Paris/Marseille. You should also change the search bar in Company Shops so they won’t be case sensitive and need full words. If you need Staff, find trusty willing players that already know the game and how it works. Many of Uwo Veterans would be super happy to be able to be part of UWO team for no advantages or payment. Make Piracy not a waste of time, cause right now, it pretty much: stay near EA, SEA, sink players only for notoriety and don’t even care if I have to give him back his trade goods cause I’m not going to go back with these goods.

But most importantly, Give these founder rewards and compensations for all they did for the game over the many past years, this way they might come back to the game even after the wipe. Ideas: Give them a permanent +5 Inventory slot. +3 Permanent skill slots. Permanent % increase for skills, exp, land speed (Don’t give sailing, would make it unfair for some events). Give a Founder starter pack. Not much, just a little something that will make life easier early. Give founders a 1 time access to a convenience option. Example: A 1 time per account access to an Aphrodite Mirror + Name change for one of your characters (They both used into 1 option, so you can’t use them separately). Give founders ability to put their name in a special colors (Of course not blue, red, green or orange). Special Founders daily Login. You don’t have to put them all, just find the ones you think the community will like the most while staying reasonable but remembering they just went over a giant Wipe. Ask the community, I’m sure you’ll hear lots of good ideas.

Overall, if the Founders perks are reasonable enough, I am willing to return to the game and work again to become a top percentage adventurer. But if the perk end up being something awful like: Here’s 5 Pirate Talisman (remember that gives 50 hours of bonus at total. Compared to the amounts of months many spends, it’s just an insult) 10 ribbons and a +1 shipbuilding trinket, you might not see me again :P. Sincerely, a player who’s been there since the release date of Uwo on Gpotatoe.

We're already in trouble, and the new host hasn't even relaunched yet. According to some sources, a player (unknown who it is at this time) will be our GM. And we know how that works out. Don't be surprised when we find out it's Mr. CoolWind himself (although this time maybe he'll be upfront about it).

On one side, we've got OGP who made a player a GM so that he could abuse his power for the betterment of his friends, refused to advertise the game, literally committed theft from players in the last week of service, wiped all data and then sold it off to the highest bidder. On the other side, we have a company making promises that will never be realized, giving out crummy astro item packages to replace years worth of work and potentially thousands of dollars of input, and already keeping players in the dark about the truth to what happened to their accounts.

And we all know WHY that data was really "Lost". The reason the game did so poorly under OGP's watch is that they were poor stewards of the game by not advertising in any way/shape/form. They even held "design an advertisement" competition, and never used the winning entry on any MMORPG website, as part of the ruse! Over time, veteran players amassed a large amount of wealth, and didn't need to purchase astro items, but the lack of incoming players lead to lack of revenue. By resetting the server, OGP/Papaya (whoever is at fault here) ensured that ALL players were no longer veterans and WOULD have to spend money to regrind. If that's not shady, I don't know what is.

This is the end, folks. I give the game another 6 months, tops. There's just not enough time or people left to make it happen, and in today's gaming market, the draw for UWO is simply not sustainable. Better not to waste our time and money here.

RIP Here lies UWO, 2010-2017. May she rest in peace (pieces?).
